sources.title: Filing text 0
sources.content: the analysis of our depreciation studies .

sources.title: Filing text 1
sources.content: changes in the estimated service lives of our assets and their related depreciation rates are implemented prospectively .

sources.title: Filing text 2
sources.content: under group depreciation , the historical cost ( net of salvage ) of depreciable property that is retired or replaced in the ordinary course of business is charged to accumulated depreciation and no gain or loss is recognized .

sources.title: Filing text 3
sources.content: the historical cost of certain track assets is estimated using ( i ) inflation indices published by the bureau of labor statistics and ( ii ) the estimated useful lives of the assets as determined by our depreciation studies .

sources.title: Filing text 4
sources.content: the indices were selected because they closely correlate with the major costs of the properties comprising the applicable track asset classes .

sources.title: Filing text 5
sources.content: because of the number of estimates inherent in the depreciation and retirement processes and because it is impossible to precisely estimate each of these variables until a group of property is completely retired , we continually monitor the estimated service lives of our assets and the accumulated depreciation associated with each asset class to ensure our depreciation rates are appropriate .

sources.title: Filing text 6
sources.content: in addition , we determine if the recorded amount of accumulated depreciation is deficient ( or in excess ) of the amount indicated by our depreciation studies .

sources.title: Filing text 7
sources.content: any deficiency ( or excess ) is amortized as a component of depreciation expense over the remaining service lives of the applicable classes of assets .

sources.title: Filing text 8
sources.content: for retirements of depreciable railroad properties that do not occur in the normal course of business , a gain or loss may be recognized if the retirement meets each of the following three conditions : ( i ) is unusual , ( ii ) is material in amount , and ( iii ) varies significantly from the retirement profile identified through our depreciation studies .

sources.title: Filing text 9
sources.content: a gain or loss is recognized in other income when we sell land or dispose of assets that are not part of our railroad operations .

sources.title: Filing text 10
sources.content: when we purchase an asset , we capitalize all costs necessary to make the asset ready for its intended use .

sources.title: Filing text 11
sources.content: however , many of our assets are self-constructed .

sources.title: Filing text 12
sources.content: a large portion of our capital expenditures is for replacement of existing track assets and other road properties , which is typically performed by our employees , and for track line expansion and other capacity projects .

sources.title: Filing text 13
sources.content: costs that are directly attributable to capital projects ( including overhead costs ) are capitalized .

sources.title: Filing text 14
